strings.name: Eliud Kipchoge
strings.role: Distance runner · Two-time Olympic marathon champion
strings.summary: Kipchoge moved from a world 5000m title to road marathons, winning two Olympic marathon golds and twice setting the world record of the time. His sub-two-hour run in a specially arranged 2019 challenge widened public interest in distance running; it must be distinguished from an official world record. He won the Melbourne Marathon in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Research checked through 13 November 2026, with selected events through October 2026. The 2019 sub-two-hour challenge was a specially arranged exhibition; the 2018 and 2022 marks were world records at the time.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Back-to-back Olympic marathons
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Won marathon gold at Rio 2016 and at the Tokyo Games held in 2021.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Two world records
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Ran 2:01:39 in 2018 and 2:01:09 in 2022, each a marathon world record at the time.
strings.highlights.highlight-03.title: Sub-two-hour challenge
strings.highlights.highlight-03.text: Ran 1:59:40.2 in Vienna in 2019 under special conditions that made it ineligible as an official world record.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Wins Melbourne Marathon
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Won in 2:09:10, setting a race record.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Improves the world record
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Ran 2:01:09 in Berlin, taking 30 seconds off his own previous world record.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Defends Olympic marathon title
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Won the Tokyo Olympic marathon in Sapporo, completing consecutive Olympic victories.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Sub-two-hour exhibition
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Completed the INEOS challenge in Vienna in 1:59:40.2; the performance was not eligible for world-record ratification.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: First marathon world record
strings.timeline.event-06.title: First Olympic marathon gold
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Winning marathon debut
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Won his first official marathon in Hamburg in 2:05:30.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Beijing 5000m silver
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Continued his track career with Olympic silver in the men’s 5000m.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: World 5000m champion
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Won the men’s 5000m at the World Championships in Paris.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Kenya
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Grew up in Kenya and later moved from track distance running to road marathons.
